Study Scheme
 
Natural Sciences

Natural Sciences

Applicable to students admitted in 2025-26

 

 

Major Programme Requirement (for Associate Degree or Higher Diploma holders admitted to senior-year places)

 

Students are required to complete a minimum of 51 units of courses as follows:

 

Students must choose one concentration area and take at least 32 units of courses (including at least 3 units of research course(s)) among the subject areas prescribed under required courses and corresponding concentration area courses, namely Biological Sciences, Biotechnology, Environmental Studies, Food and Nutrition, Data Science, Chemical and Testing Sciences, and Physical Sciences.  Students will fulfill this unit requirement automatically by taking the relevant courses as prescribed in each concentration area.  Upon completion of all courses prescribed under a concentration area, the concentration area will be printed on academic transcript.

These courses if not taken to fulfill the requirement as prescribed in Required Courses can be taken to fulfill the requirement as prescribed in Elective Courses.

[b]

Students should take the required number of units of Elective Courses (Item 2) in accordance with the units completed in Required Courses (Item 1) to fulfill the 51 units of courses of Major Programme Requirement.

[c]

Students taking PHYS1002 instead of PHYS1111 may not be able to take some of the PHYS courses because PHYS1111 is a prerequisite for some Physics courses.

[d]

Students may, with written approval by the Natural Sciences Programme, use one or more of the following courses to substitute those listed:

MATH2055, 2070, 2230, 3010, 3230, 3240, 4220

Study Scheme
Learning Outcomes
 

Upon completion of the Natural Sciences Programme,

 

1.

Knowledge (K)

(1)

General Science Knowledge

Graduates will have acquired the ability to:

·                      

Demonstrate a broad understanding of fundamental scientific principles across disciplines (K1) ; and

·                      

Explain scientific methodologies, experimental design, and analytical techniques, and describe their applications in scientific research (K2) .

 

 

(2)

Concentration-Specific Knowledge

Graduates will have acquired in-depth knowledge in one of the following areas (K3):

·                      

Biological Sciences:

 

Comprehensive understanding of the core concepts in genetics, molecular, cell biology, microbiology, ecology, biodiversity, evolution, and physiology.

·                      

Biotechnology:

 

Knowledge of biochemistry, medical, genetic engineering, and microbial, plant, and animal biotechnology in research and industry.

·                      

Environmental Studies:

 

In-depth understanding of environmental science principles, sustainability challenges and conservation strategies.

·                      

Food and Nutrition:

 

Expertise in human nutrition, food safety, food chemical and technology, dietary planning, and the biochemical basis of nutrition and health.

·          

Data Science:

 

Proficiency in statistical modeling, mathematical tools, and machine learning for scientific analysis.

·                      

Chemical and Testing Sciences:

 

Strong foundation in analytical techniques in chemical analysis, materials testing, and quality control.

·                      

Physical Sciences:

 

Knowledge of fundamental physics principles and their applications in scientific and technological problem-solving.

 

2.

 

Skills (S)

Students will have been equipped the ability to:

·                      

apply scientific knowledge and analytical skills to solve problems (S1);

·                      

communicate scientific information effectively (S2);

·                      

collaborate and work effectively in teams (S3); and

·                      

integrate knowledge and adapt to global perspectives (S4).

 

3.

 

Values & Attitudes (V)

Students will have been nurtured virtues that are conducive to good personal ethics, such as:

·                      

demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility (V1);

·                      

contribute to society and address global challenges (V2); and

·                      

engage in lifelong lLearning (V3).
